team.summary: Solo founder Tom Morkes (COO) brings 3x founder experience, West Point background, and GTM leadership for hundreds of launches. Strong founder-market fit for B2B SaaS go-to-market, but no technical co-founder or in-house AI/ML depth is evident.

founders.name: Tom Morkes
founders.background: 3x founder, West Point graduate, led GTM for hundreds of launches generating millions in revenue; currently COO at Helply.

team.technicalDepth: [inferred] No technical founder or CTO mentioned; core AI/integration layer likely relies on third-party LLMs rather than proprietary models.

product.plainLanguage: An AI-native helpdesk and support agent that automatically resolves customer tickets end-to-end for small B2B SaaS teams, with a free unlimited-seat helpdesk and outcome-based AI pricing.
product.category: AI customer support agent / helpdesk automation

market.sizeHint: [inferred] Small B2B SaaS companies — a large but fragmented segment; no specific TAM/SAM figures disclosed.
market.competitiveLandscape: Competes with well-funded incumbents (Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI, Gorgias) and a wave of vertical AI support agents (e.g., Decagon, Sierra, Forethought). Helply's wedge is a free unlimited-seat helpdesk plus outcome-based AI pricing.
market.whyNow: LLM cost collapse makes autonomous support agents affordable for small teams; rising ticket volumes and hiring constraints create urgency for automation.

risks.text: Thin LLM wrapper with no proprietary data or model differentiation; defensibility relies on workflow lock-in that may be weak for small teams.
No technical founder or in-house AI capability; dependent on horizontal LLM providers for core intelligence.
Crowded market with deep-pocketed incumbents and better-funded vertical specialists; customer acquisition may be expensive.
Traction signals are limited to self-published blog content; no independent verification of paying customers, usage, or revenue.

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Strong founder-market fit for B2B SaaS GTM (3x founder, West Point, launch experience) but missing technical depth to own the core AI/integration layer; no evidence of prior exits.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: No proprietary data or model mentioned; differentiation appears to be pricing (free helpdesk + outcome-based AI) and vertical focus, which are replicable. Likely dependent on a single horizontal LLM platform.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: Clear one-sentence value prop; AI-native agent (end-to-end ticket resolution) not just a copilot; self-serve onboarding implied for SMBs. Product vision aligns well with thesis.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Specific vertical (small B2B SaaS support) with credible why-now drivers (LLM cost drop, hiring pain). However, market size hint is vague and competitive landscape is intense with established players.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Only signal is a self-published blog post listing Helply among '15 best AI agents'; no paying customer count, revenue, funding, launch metrics, or third-party validation. Freshness unknown.

scoreRationale: Helply shows product clarity and founder GTM experience, but lacks technical depth, proprietary moat, and verifiable traction. The market is attractive but crowded. Weighted sub-scores reflect a below-average overall profile for the thesis.
